verdict.rationale: Unity's core product, the Editor and Player, is installed and run on the user's own machines. The docs cover installing Editors on your own CI/build agents with the Unity CLI and running headless via command-line arguments, so users can run the core on their own infrastructure. However, the evidence frames this as locally installed proprietary software, not a documented self-hosting deployment, and community reports describe the engine depending on phoning home to Unity. Missing for 10: explicit self-hosting/offline-operation documentation, self-hostable equivalents of Unity's hosted services (AI Assistant credits, Build Automation), open source or redistributable core, independent corroboration of fully self-contained operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Use the Unity CLI to install and manage Unity Editors and modules from the command-line... Use it for new scripts, automation, and CI pipelines.
